## It does not balance, and it is not supposed to yet

A reconciliation that always balances is not being computed. These are
the reasons this one does not, in order of size:

**1 · The roster is incomplete.** `roster_complete` is `False`. The roster
is built a page at a time inside a rate limit and is not finished, so
the live count is a lower bound that rises on every run. This is the
dominant term and it shrinks by itself.

**2 · The two sources count different things.** The frozen IDB is a
case-level administrative record of every civil case reported to the
Administrative Office. RECAP holds what somebody purchased or
contributed from PACER. Neither is a subset of the other.

**3 · The freeze lags.** The IDB is refreshed quarterly and this
snapshot was taken 2026-08-26; a case filed last week is in RECAP and
not in the freeze. The live edge is, by construction, ahead.

**4 · Nature of suit is coded differently.** The frozen source stores a
three-digit code. The live source stores free text that happens to
begin with it. `istartswith` bridges them and would not survive a court
that formats the field differently.

**`UNCLASSIFIED` is 84.0% and that is a health metric, not a bug.**
Most of it is entries with no description text at all — RECAP holds
the docket line without the document. They are retained and counted
rather than dropped, because an entry with no text is still evidence
that something happened, and discarding it would silently shrink
every denominator. See `docket-event-derivation.md` D-04 and D-05.

A run that stops early because the rate limit bound it is recorded as
stopped, not as failed, and it says which window bound it. A run that
fails an assertion is recorded as failed and publishes which one. The
distinction is deliberate: a pipeline that reports designed
backpressure as failure trains its reader to ignore red.
